candidate_relations.reason: The clinical and histological features described — reddish-brown hyperkeratotic papules with bleeding on scale removal, compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate — are characteristic of Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans (Flegel disease). Necrobiosis Lipoidica presents with yellowish-brown atrophic plaques with telangiectasias and histologically shows palisading granulomas with necrobiosis of collagen, not compact hyperkeratosis with bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate. Although both conditions can be associated with diabetes mellitus, they are entirely different diagnostic entities.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Necrobiosis Lipoidica is a distinct granulomatous dermatosis associated with diabetes, not the same entity as Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans (Flegel disease)

case_quality_flags: Unilateral presentation of HLP is an atypical but documented variant; the reference diagnosis appropriately specifies this qualifier
Diabetes mellitus association noted in both the case and candidate C001, but does not support diagnostic equivalence
